quote: Theorem 4. Let X_i ~ GaL(alpha_i, beta_i), i = 1, 2, be two random variables. If alpha_1 = alpha_2 = alpha and beta_1 <= beta_2, ... then X1 ~lr X2 => X1 ~hr X2 => X1 ~st X2. [Proof:] ... if alpha_1 = alpha_2 = alpha, then X1 is stochastically smaller than X2 with respect to the likelihood ratio if and only if beta_1 <= beta_2.
family: GaL(alpha, beta): compound gamma-Lindley, pdf f(x) = alpha beta^2 (1 + alpha + beta + x) x^{alpha-1} / [(1+beta)(beta+x)^{2+alpha}], x > 0, alpha, beta > 0
compared: two GaL variables with common alpha, ordered beta

hypotheses.text: alpha_1 = alpha_2 = alpha and beta_1 <= beta_2

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_lr X2 (hence <=_hr and <=_st); iff according to proof

ambiguity: Printed as a single joint statement combining both cases; this record captures the common-alpha case, proved as an iff via q(beta) decreasing.

quote: If beta_1 = beta_2 = beta >= 1 with alpha_1 <= alpha_2, then X1 ~lr X2 => X1 ~hr X2 => X1 ~st X2. [Proof:] Hence, if beta_1 = beta_2 = beta >= 1, then X1 is stochastically smaller than X2 with respect to the likelihood ratio if and only if alpha_1 <= alpha_2.
compared: two GaL variables with common beta >= 1, ordered alpha

hypotheses.text: beta_1 = beta_2 = beta >= 1 and alpha_1 <= alpha_2

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_lr X2 (hence <=_hr and <=_st); iff according to proof

ambiguity: Restriction beta >= 1 is needed for du(alpha)/dalpha > 0 in the proof.
